correctness.rationale: The Hamming transport unit ball is the convex hull of oriented unit-edge molecules. An explicit two-valued Lipschitz potential proves that parallel edges form an isometric ell-one family. Independent-coordinate convolution yields exactly the indicated signed edge coefficients. All rates, dimensions and time boundaries are covered; derivative monotonicity and a uniform logarithmic expansion establish uniqueness and the sharp peak asymptotic. Forty-eight exhaustive small-cube integral Lipschitz-dual comparisons, 360 exact rational anisotropic shadow identities, and 70 separate numerical transport LP diagnostics corroborate the result without serving as the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The transient distance profile and universal dimension-three overshoot threshold concern non-idempotent heat multipliers and their temporal maxima. No inspected source states or logically implies the peak law as a special case of its published theorem. The published Walsh spectral projection result supplies a closely related edge-shadow method but has only zero-one spectral multipliers; adapting its proof to heat multipliers is possible, so the method itself is not independently claimed. The novel mathematical content retained is the all-rate explicit heat-distance formula together with the sharp temporal peak and logarithmic large-dimension law. Earlier equivalent Markov semigroup norm estimates remain a real bibliographic risk.
residual_risks: A general Fourier-multiplier shadow formula could imply the exact heat norm after substitution; the earlier published projection proof can be adapted, even though its theorem does not state that generalization.
Equivalent transient norm profiles might have been published using Wasserstein-one, earthmover, Kantorovich-Rubinstein or Dobrushin coefficient nomenclature.
Searches and inspections do not prove uniqueness or independent scientific validation.

value.rationale: This identifies a natural semigroup phenomenon absent in dimensions one and two but inevitable in every higher-dimensional Boolean cube for all heterogeneous positive rates: the distance from identity transiently exceeds its long-time limit 1. The isotropic extremal norm approaches the sharp triangle-inequality ceiling 2, with a logarithmic peak time and a two-term height defect. The object, invariant and phase transition are intrinsic to the standard Hamming transport geometry rather than an arbitrary finite numerical slice.
